key_insight: A two-step screening workflow—automated EHR flagging followed by structured non-physician chart review—substantially narrows a large candidate pool to a higher-yield prospective sepsis cohort.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve efficiency for enrolling well-characterized sepsis patients for biomarker and host-response studies, while reducing burden on clinical teams and study staff.
method: Automated EHR screening for SIRS criteria, microbiologic testing, and new antibiotic use
Structured enrichment review by trained non-physician staff
Primary team discussion plus physician adjudication into diagnostic categories
evidence_signal: In 4,318 screened patients, 1,220 (28%) were flagged and 288 enrolled; among enrolled patients, 73% were adjudicated as sepsis, supporting enrichment of the final cohort.
watch_item: The workflow may improve cohort quality but still depends on local EHR data capture, staff expertise, and site-specific adjudication practices, which could limit generalizability.
paper_title: Efficiency of a Multi-step Screening and Enrichment Process for Prospective Sepsis Cohort Enrollment
